questions.question: A device that converts AC to DC using switching elements is called?
questions.tutor: Rectifier uses diodes or thyristors to convert AC to DC for power supplies, battery chargers, and DC drives.

questions.question: The component that converts DC to AC is known as?
questions.tutor: Inverter uses switching devices (IGBT, MOSFET) to produce AC from DC source like battery or solar panel.

questions.question: A chopper circuit performs which type of conversion?
questions.tutor: Chopper (DC-DC converter) changes DC voltage level by switching at high frequency.

questions.question: A cycloconverter directly converts?
questions.tutor: Cycloconverter converts fixed frequency AC to variable frequency AC without intermediate DC link.

questions.question: The semiconductor device most commonly used in modern inverters for motor drives is?
questions.tutor: IGBT combines high voltage capability of BJT with fast switching of MOSFET; dominant in VFDs and inverters.

questions.question: A device that combines a rectifier, DC link, and inverter in one unit for motor speed control is called?
questions.tutor: VFD controls induction motor speed by varying frequency and voltage output.

questions.question: The main advantage of a PWM (Pulse Width Modulation) inverter over a square wave inverter is?
questions.tutor: PWM reduces harmonic content, producing near-sinusoidal current with minimal filtering.

questions.question: A thyristor (SCR) turns off naturally when?
questions.tutor: SCR is a latching device; it turns off only when anode current drops below holding current (natural commutation).

questions.question: For a 3-phase full-bridge rectifier with ideal diodes, the output ripple frequency is?
questions.tutor: Three-phase full-bridge rectifier produces 6 pulses per cycle, so ripple frequency = 6 × f = 360 Hz.

questions.question: A buck converter produces an output voltage that is?
questions.tutor: Buck converter (step-down DC-DC) uses switching and filtering to reduce voltage.

questions.question: A boost converter produces an output voltage that is?
questions.tutor: Boost converter steps up DC voltage by storing energy in inductor and releasing it to output.

questions.question: The component that provides DC link voltage smoothing in a VFD is typically?
questions.tutor: DC link capacitor filters rectified voltage and provides low-impedance source for inverter.

questions.question: A device that protects electronic power equipment from voltage spikes is called?
questions.tutor: Metal Oxide Varistor (MOV) clamps transient overvoltages to safe levels.

questions.question: In a power supply, the component that stores energy and smooths output ripple is?
questions.tutor: Capacitor (or LC filter) smooths rectified output by charging during peaks and discharging during valleys.

questions.question: A switching power supply operates at high frequency to?
questions.tutor: Higher frequency allows smaller magnetic components, reducing cost and size of power supplies.

questions.question: The typical switching frequency range for IGBTs in industrial VFDs is?
questions.tutor: IGBTs in VFDs typically switch 2-16 kHz; higher frequency reduces audible noise but increases losses.

questions.question: A regenerative drive returns energy from the motor back to?
questions.tutor: Regenerative drive feeds braking energy back to utility, saving energy compared to resistor braking.

questions.question: The purpose of a braking chopper in a VFD is?
choices: Dissipate excess regenerative energy in resistor
questions.tutor: Braking chopper dumps excess DC link voltage from regeneration into a dynamic braking resistor.

questions.question: A device that converts fixed voltage DC to variable voltage DC using high-frequency switching and isolation is called?
questions.tutor: SMPS uses flyback, forward, or push-pull topologies to provide regulated isolated DC output.

questions.question: The main loss mechanism in a switching device (IGBT/MOSFET) during turn-on and turn-off is?
questions.tutor: Switching loss occurs due to simultaneous voltage and current overlap during transitions.

questions.question: A power factor correction (PFC) circuit in a power supply primarily reduces?
questions.tutor: Active PFC shapes input current to follow voltage waveform, improving power factor and reducing harmonics.

questions.question: The component used to isolate control circuit from power circuit in a switching supply is?
questions.tutor: Optocoupler (light) or pulse transformer provides galvanic isolation between primary and secondary sides.

questions.question: A soft starter differs from a VFD because it?
choices: Only reduces starting current, no speed control
questions.tutor: Soft starter reduces voltage during start to limit inrush; once at full speed, it bypasses to line.

questions.question: The term 'dead time' in an inverter bridge refers to?
choices: Delay between switching off one device and turning on complementary device
questions.tutor: Dead time prevents shoot-through (simultaneous conduction) of upper and lower switches in inverter leg.

questions.question: A device that converts AC to AC at the same frequency but different voltage using back-to-back thyristors is?
questions.tutor: AC voltage controller uses triacs or anti-parallel SCRs to vary RMS voltage by phase-angle control.
